summary: Summation No. 23 covers August 1947 (many statistics are for July or June), in the second year of the Occupation. Politically it records the creation of a Ministry of Labor on 28 August under Mitsusuke Yonekubo, the Katayama Cabinet's coal-control dispute with the Liberal Party, which scrapped the Four-party Agreement on 12 August, Prime Minister Katayama's 17 August appeal to the nation, and Councillor by-elections. A long analysis of the April 1947 elections gives vote counts, Purge screening, women candidates and campaign finance. Legal sections report the new Supreme Court and war crimes trials, including Pacific-phase tribunal testimony. Economic sections give production, labor, trade, rationing, price-control, banking and property-custody figures, with floods, coal shortfalls and first postwar foreign-trade shipments. Social sections cover epidemic disease, textbooks and media. The appendix reviews the second Occupation year (1 September 1946 to 31 August 1947), a useful overview for historians. The scan ends at printed page 336, so the Map of Japan is the last item.
highlights: A Ministry of Labor was established on 28 August under Social Democrat Mitsusuke Yonekubo, its first Minister, after the Labor Ministry Law passed on 29 August; it handles all labor matters except those of seamen.
The Liberal Party scrapped the Four-party Agreement on 12 August and went into opposition; Secretary General Banboku Ono announced on 23 August a movement to overthrow the Katayama Cabinet.

Coal control caused wide political controversy: the Democrats announced a 19-point program on 4 August, opposed by the People's Cooperative and Social Democratic Parties, while the July coal quota was beaten by 10,300 metric tons.

In the April 1947 local elections, independents won 9,257 of 10,419 mayoralties, 31 of 46 governorships and 173,999 of 193,881 assembly seats; ten of 19 women candidates won House of Councillors seats.

The first Supreme Court under the new Constitution was organized with a Chief Justice and 14 associate justices; war crimes work completed 12 trials of 37 persons, with 4 acquitted and 33 sentenced to 18 months to life.

First agricultural land sales under the Land Reform law were completed, with tenants buying 24,325 cho (59,621 acres) in 12 prefectures; northern Honshu flood damage was estimated above 7,000,000,000 yen.

Foreign trade reopened: cotton fabrics went to 19 countries in July (68,138,000 linear yards), the first postwar Davao hemp arrived from the Philippines, and Bank of Japan notes in circulation reached 150,684,000,000 yen on 31 August.

Mitsui Trading and Mitsubishi Trading began liquidation under the Holding Company Liquidation Commission, with operating loans of 200,000,000 and 120,000,000 yen; the Reconstruction Finance Bank had lent 17,982,000,000 yen.

sections.title: Front matter
sections.summary: Cover for Summation No. 23 (August 1947), table of contents, and list of 106 charts, maps and graphs, from industrial production indexes to the Map of Japan.

sections.title: Part I: General
sections.summary: Monthly digest: no SCAP reorganization, new Ministry of Labor, coal-control politics, first land-reform sales, steel and trade gains, rationing, finance and property control.

sections.title: Section 1. Organization Under SCAP
sections.summary: Reports no change in the organization of General Headquarters, SCAP, during August 1947.

sections.title: Section 2. Political Activities
sections.summary: Ministry of Labor created 28 August; Katayama's 17 August appeal; party reactions to coal control; April election analysis; Purge Appeal Board members named to the Supreme Court; juvenile police departments; war crimes figures.

sections.title: Section 3. Economic Activities
sections.summary: First land-reform sales, northern Honshu floods, July coal quota beaten by 10,300 tons, steel and aluminum gains, first Davao hemp, note circulation of 150,684,000,000 yen, and property custody.

sections.title: Section 4. Social Activities
sections.summary: Disease rates kept falling apart from malaria and dysentery; Hokkaido residents got first typhus inoculations; welfare payments rose from 1 July; 60,000+ repatriates arrived; teacher workshops prepared for compulsory handicapped schooling in April 1948.

sections.title: Part II: Political
sections.summary: Covers the new Ministry of Labor, coal control, parties, the Diet, the April 1947 elections, public safety statistics, the new Supreme Court and war crimes trials.

sections.title: Section 1. Government and Politics
sections.summary: Yonekubo named Labor Minister, coal-control disputes, Liberal break with the coalition, Communist and Democratic Party positions, and a long analysis of the April 1947 elections with vote tables.

sections.title: Administration and Political Developments
sections.summary: Ministry of Labor creation, coal control, House of Councillors by-elections in five prefectures, food release, and Prime Minister Katayama's 17 August appeal to the nation.

sections.title: Political Parties
sections.summary: Democratic 19-point coal plan; Liberal sponsorship of the All-Japan Farmers' Union on 3 August and break with the coalition on 12 August; Communist attacks on the Cabinet.

sections.title: The Diet
sections.summary: Joint Legislative Committee (10 representatives, eight councillors) met 26 August under chairman Senso Higai; standing committees did field studies and held two public hearings on Criminal and Civil Code bills; free debates covered housing and rice.

sections.title: Analysis of the April Elections
sections.summary: April 1947 elections: laws, Purge screening, publicity, local and national results, women's participation, abstention rates and campaign financing, with vote charts.

sections.title: The Purge
sections.summary: As of 27 August, committees had screened 590,130 persons since 4 January; 1,548 central officials removed. Tanaka and Yamamoto were cleared on appeal, media screening reached 330 cases, and four Purge Appeal Board members joined the Supreme Court.

sections.title: Section 2. Public Safety
sections.summary: Railway casualties, criminal offenses by prefecture, police juvenile departments, prison population of 78,147 in July, and June fire losses of 226,738,226 yen.

sections.title: Section 3. Legal Affairs and War Crimes
sections.summary: Organization of the first Supreme Court under the new Constitution; 79 new suspects ordered arrested; 1,089 held in Sugamo; tribunal testimony on Pacific-phase, diplomatic and naval planning.

sections.title: Part III: Economic
sections.summary: July and August 1947 statistics on production, labor, trade, prices, finance and property across twelve economic sections, with charts and tables.

sections.title: Section 1. Agriculture and Fisheries
sections.summary: Tenant purchases of 24,325 cho of land, 269,943 cho received for taxes, northern Honshu flood damage, July fish catch and fishing vessel fuel allotments.

sections.title: Section 2. Forestry and Mining
sections.summary: Log output fell in July; coal beat its quota by 10,300 tons then declined in August; also firewood, charcoal, camphor, stockpiles, lignite and the Imperial Oil Company's new well.

sections.title: Section 3. Heavy Industries
sections.summary: July coke output was 172,500 metric tons, up 19,000; rolled steel rose five percent to 53,358 tons; cement 100,597 tons; chemical production index hit 48 percent of requirements; machine tools 635 units; rolling stock fell 26 percent.

sections.title: Section 4. Manufacturing
sections.summary: July food fats and oils rose to 3,036 metric tons from 1,737; sake fell to 414 hectoliters, beer rose to 90,686; bicycles reached a postwar high of 18,069; sewing machines 6,860; matches hit a yearly high.

sections.title: Section 5. Textile Industries
sections.summary: July cotton yarn fell to 25,285,000 pounds from June's postwar peak of 29,004,000 as raw cotton ran short; rayon filament yarn and rayon pulp rose to a postwar peak; raw silk reached 9,281 bales; wool output slipped.

sections.title: Section 6. Transportation and Public Utilities
sections.summary: Electric power generation of 3,482,000 kW with water availability at 112 percent of average; June consumption of 2,112,100,000 kWh; also motor, rail, coastal and foreign shipping, and gas.

sections.title: Section 7. Communications
sections.summary: August: radiotelegraph and international mail opened to commercial traffic (25 August) and air mail authorized 28 August; about 12,000 new telephones in July; JT&T staff moved to the Ministry; 120 postal construction projects completed.

sections.title: Section 8. Labor
sections.summary: Labor Ministry Law passed 29 August; 72 disputes involving 45,223 workers in June; Central Labor Relations Committee ruling; union membership, wage demands, labor schools and Occupation labor.

sections.title: Section 9. Imports and Exports
sections.summary: July cotton fabric exports of 68,138,000 yards to 19 countries and first postwar Philippine Davao hemp, plus food, machinery, chemicals and metals trade.

sections.title: Section 10. Rationing and Price Control
sections.summary: Full month's ration for the nine largest cities, potato and summer-grain collections, controls on processed fish and vegetables, producers' goods price rises and urban family expenditures.

sections.title: Section 11. Finance
sections.summary: Note circulation of 150,684,000,000 yen; Reconstruction Finance Bank loans of 17,982,000,000 yen; Japan Securities Exchange offering of 945,000 shares; national debt of 300,882,000,000 yen.

sections.title: Section 12. Property Control and Reparations
sections.summary: Foreign nationals' property of 1,399,909,000 yen, war suspects' property of 85,377,000 yen, Mitsui and Mitsubishi Trading liquidation, Hayashikaze restricted, and 147 plants inspected for reparations.

sections.title: Part IV: Social
sections.summary: August 1947 social report: communicable disease and DDT campaigns, medical supply output, relief for 2,656,538 persons, repatriation of 60,850; teacher workshops, O-bon, radio fee rise to ¥17.50, press comment; appendix opens.

sections.title: Section 1. Public Health and Welfare
sections.summary: Murine typhus in 12 prefectures; Hokkaido vaccination reached 991,803; July hospitals 3,371; penicillin output fell to 175,290,000 units; relief paid ¥234,158,053 to 2,656,538 persons; 60,850 repatriated; June births 197,747.

sections.title: Section 2. Education, Religion and Media of Expression
sections.summary: Handicapped-teacher workshop ended 22 August with 159 teachers; Ibaraki upper-secondary survey; O-bon festivals; monument removal in Tokyo; radio license fee raised to ¥17.50; press on Katayama Cabinet and foreign trade; Coizumi Studio founded.

sections.title: Appendix: Review of the Second Occupation Year, 1 September 1946 - 31 August 1947
sections.summary: Review of the second Occupation year (1 September 1946 to 31 August 1947): food, inflation, democratization, labor, industry, trade, communications, finance, property control and reparations.

sections.title: Section 1. Organization under SCAP
sections.summary: Two new special staff sections were set up in GHQ in the second Occupation year: Civil Transportation Section (7 September 1946) and Reparations Section (8 May 1947), plus a Reparations Technical Advisory Committee (21 May 1947).

sections.title: Section 2. Securing of Necessities of Life
sections.summary: Food imports and the summer food crisis, land reclamation, shelter, the White Paper and stabilization program against inflation, and public welfare and health.

sections.title: Section 3. Progress of Democratization
sections.summary: New Constitution, 1947 elections, Purge, courts, International Military Tribunal and Class B and C trials, agrarian reform, labor, antitrust, education, religion and media.

sections.title: Section 4. Economic Progress
sections.summary: Year's progress in coal, heavy industry, textiles, trade, transport, communications and finance (Reconstruction Finance Bank 17,982,000,000 yen); reparations committee set up May 1947.
